group: shell/* and util/* (packages/shell/shell, shell/shell-env, shell/bash-local, shell/bash-sandbox, shell/pwsh-local, shell/pwsh-sandbox, shell/tool-bash, shell/tool-bash-persistent, shell/tool-pwsh, shell/tool-pwsh-persistent, util/native-command, util/timeout)

mechanisms.name: shell-executor-service-seam
mechanisms.what: `ShellExecutor` is an abstract Cordis `Service` registered under the name `shell` (`ctx.shell`), declared via module augmentation of `Context` (index.ts:39-43). It defines three abstract members: `resolve(request): ShellExecSpec` (index.ts:84), `run(spec): Promise<ShellRunResult>` (index.ts:92) and `start(spec): ShellProcess` (index.ts:99), plus a `sandboxMode` getter that defaults to `undefined` (index.ts:74-76). The settings namespace constant `SHELL_SETTINGS_NAMESPACE = 'shell'` is owned here (index.ts:21) so bash and pwsh providers share one namespace without double registration.
invariants: `run` rejects only for infrastructure failures. Nonzero exits, timeout kills, and abort kills resolve with a `ShellRunResult`. (packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts:52-53)

`start` returns immediately; no timeout applies to background processes. `done` settles at process close and never rejects; spawn failures settle as `killed` with the error on stderr. (packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts:54-56)
`ShellProcess.readOutput` is incremental: consecutive reads never repeat output. Lossy reads report truncation and available spill files. (packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts:57-58)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — loading a second provider of `ctx.shell` throws (cordis duplicate-service behaviour, stated as fact at packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts:48-49 and :15-18); `resolve`/`run`/`start` are abstract so a provider cannot silently no-op.

constants.meaning: SHELL_SETTINGS_NAMESPACE, the settings section both executor families install into
service name passed to super(ctx, 'shell')

mechanisms.name: shell-request-resolution-and-caps
mechanisms.what: `LocalBashExecutor.resolve()` / `PwshLocalExecutor.resolve()` fill and clamp a `ShellExecRequest` into a `ShellExecSpec`: `timeoutMs` via `clampTimeout(request.timeoutMs, config.timeoutMs, config.maxTimeoutMs, '<impl>: request.timeoutMs')`, `workdir` from `config.cwd ?? process.cwd()`, and `stdoutMaxBytes` from `request.stdoutMaxBytes ?? config.maxOutputBytes` (re-validated positive-finite). `stdin`, `env`, `dshEnv` and `sandboxPolicy` are carried through verbatim with no defaults. `clampTimeout` implements `Math.min(requested ?? def, max)` and rejects a non-finite or non-positive hint.
invariants: The tool layer calls this before run/start, so those methods receive explicit values and never re-default. (packages/shell/bash-local/src/index.ts:145-147)
`timeoutMs` is filled from `config.timeoutMs`, capped at `config.maxTimeoutMs`. (packages/shell/bash-local/src/index.ts:144-145)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — negative, zero or non-finite values throw (`bash-local: request.timeoutMs must be a positive finite number` via packages/util/timeout/src/index.ts:51-53 and `assertPositiveFinite` at packages/shell/bash-local/src/index.ts:69-73); a caller-supplied value is silently capped (not rejected) at `maxTimeoutMs`.

constants.meaning: default `timeoutMs` (schema default) — pwsh identical at packages/shell/pwsh-local/src/index.ts:133
default `maxTimeoutMs` cap — pwsh identical at packages/shell/pwsh-local/src/index.ts:134
default `maxOutputBytes` per stream (in-memory cap) — pwsh identical at packages/shell/pwsh-local/src/index.ts:135
DEFAULT_MAX_SPILL_BYTES, the per-stream spill-file cap
DEFAULT_GRACE_MS, the SIGTERM->SIGKILL grace period

mechanisms.name: shell-service-config-validation
mechanisms.what: `assertServiceableBashConfig` and its pwsh twin re-validate a schema-valid config section at the point it is written (constructor and settings `validate` hook): `timeoutMs`, `maxTimeoutMs`, `maxOutputBytes`, `maxSpillBytes`, `graceMs` must each be positive and finite, and `graceMs` must be `<= MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS`. The executors install the section into the shared `shell` settings namespace with `ctx.inject(['settings'], ... installSection(ctx, SHELL_SETTINGS_NAMESPACE, Config, entry, {validate, setSource, onChange}))`.
invariants: a stored value is refused where it is written instead of failing at the next command. (packages/shell/bash-local/src/index.ts:78-80)
`graceMs` must be no greater than `2147483647`. (packages/shell/bash-local/src/index.ts:90-92)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — throws `Error` naming the offending field (`bash-local: <name> must be a positive finite number`).

constants.meaning: MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS — largest delay Node schedules without clamping to 1 ms; also the `graceMs` upper bound at packages/shell/bash-local/src/index.ts:90 and packages/shell/pwsh-local/src/index.ts:118

mechanisms.name: shell-terminal-env-overrides
mechanisms.what: Each executor exports an `ENV_OVERRIDES` record of model-friendly terminal settings that is spread first into the spawn environment, so a trusted caller's own entry still wins. bash uses `NO_COLOR: '1'`, `TERM: 'dumb'`, `PAGER: 'cat'`, `GIT_PAGER: 'cat'`; pwsh deliberately omits `TERM` because it is a POSIX concept. The final map is `{ ...ENV_OVERRIDES, ...spec.env, ...spec.dshEnv }`, i.e. managed `DSH_*` beats caller env beats overrides.
invariants: merged first into the spawn's explicit env, so a trusted caller's own entry still wins (packages/shell/bash-local/src/index.ts:24-26)
`TERM=dumb` is a POSIX concept and is deliberately absent (packages/shell/pwsh-local/src/index.ts:31-32)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-open — these are plain default entries; nothing verifies that the child honours them, and a caller env entry silently displaces any of them.

constants.meaning: disable coloured output
bash-only; absent from the pwsh override set at packages/shell/pwsh-local/src/index.ts:34-38
disable pagers that would garble tool output

mechanisms.name: pwsh-executable-resolution
mechanisms.what: `resolvePwshPath(configured, env, platform)` returns `configured` untouched when non-empty; otherwise on win32 it probes `candidatePwshPaths(env)` in order — `$ProgramFiles\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe`, then `pwsh.exe` under each clean PATH entry (quotes stripped), then `$SystemRoot\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe` — accepting the first candidate for which `lstatSync` reports `isFile()` OR `isSymbolicLink()`; if none exists (or the platform is not win32) it returns the bare string `'pwsh'` for PATH resolution. `PwshLocalExecutor` re-resolves only when the declared `pwshPath` actually changes, via the settings `onChange` hook.
invariants: resolution is a pure function of its inputs on every platform (packages/shell/pwsh-local/src/resolve.ts:16-18)
a probe that resolved differently from the code under test could exempt a file whose suites actually run. (packages/shell/pwsh-local/src/resolve.ts:4-6)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft — a missing/unprobeable candidate is skipped and resolution degrades to the bare `pwsh` name, deferring failure to spawn time.

constants.meaning: default `env.ProgramFiles` for the PowerShell 7 install probe
default `env.SystemRoot` for the Windows PowerShell 5.1 fallback
probed executable file names
fallback executable name left to PATH resolution

mechanisms.name: pwsh-encoding-preamble-and-command-argv
mechanisms.what: `PwshLocalExecutor.argv(spec)` builds `[this.pwshPath, '-NoLogo', '-NoProfile', '-NonInteractive', '-Command', ENCODING_PREAMBLE + spec.command]` — the whole command is ONE argv element so PowerShell itself parses it and there is no shell-quoting layer. `ENCODING_PREAMBLE` sets `[Console]::OutputEncoding` and `$OutputEncoding` to `UTF8Encoding($false)` so Windows PowerShell 5.1 (the last-resort fallback executable) does not emit OEM-codepage bytes the UTF-8 collector would garble.
invariants: The statements ride on line 1 after `; ` separators so PowerShell error line numbers stay accurate. (packages/shell/pwsh-local/src/index.ts:45-47)

The command string is passed as ONE argv element to `-Command`: PowerShell itself parses the text, and no intermediate shell exists, so there is no shell-quoting layer to escape. (packages/shell/pwsh-local/src/index.ts:8-11)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft — the preamble is prepended unconditionally; a pwsh 7 host simply re-affirms UTF-8 and nothing is validated at runtime.

constants.meaning: ENCODING_PREAMBLE prepended to every pwsh command
fixed pwsh invocation flags

mechanisms.name: sandboxed-shell-selection
mechanisms.what: `SandboxBashExecutor extends LocalBashExecutor` and `SandboxPwshExecutor extends PwshLocalExecutor` re-register as `ctx.shell` with `static inject = ['subprocess', 'sandbox', 'sandboxPolicy']` and no own Config. `resolve()` stamps `sandboxPolicy: request.sandboxPolicy ?? this.ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve()`. `run()`/`start()` read `policy.mode`; `danger-full-access` short-circuits to the unconfined super implementation (run adds `sandbox: {mode, denied:false}`), otherwise the exact local argv is wrapped by `ctx.sandbox.confine(['bash','-c',cmd] | this.argv(spec), policy)` and handed to `runArgv`/`startArgv`. The constructor reads `ctx.sandboxPolicy.defaultMode` as the advertised `sandboxMode`.
invariants: Providers may vary enforcement and diagnostic dialect between overlapping calls, so a shared latest-wrap value would classify a process against the wrong facts. (packages/shell/bash-sandbox/src/index.ts:55-57)
Once startArgv returns, install facts synchronously; promise settlement cannot run before start() returns. (packages/shell/bash-sandbox/src/index.ts:121-122)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — full-access runs unconfined (fail-open by explicit opt-in mode); a positively-identified runner failure throws `SandboxUnavailableError(mode, detail)` in the foreground (fail-closed) and stamps `runnerFailed` on a background handle; a plain denial is reported as data (`sandbox.denied`) rather than thrown.

constants.meaning: mode literal that bypasses confinement — same literal at packages/shell/pwsh-sandbox/src/index.ts:99
injected services required by the confining executor — mirrored at packages/shell/pwsh-sandbox/src/index.ts:53

mechanisms.name: sandbox-denial-and-runner-failure-classification
mechanisms.what: Two independent classifiers decide whether a settled confined run is a policy denial or a broken confinement runner. `matchesSignature(exitCode, stderr, signatures)` requires a non-null non-zero exit AND a case-insensitive stderr substring match. `classifyRunnerFailure(exitCode, stderr, rules)` requires non-zero exit, an optional `allowedExitCodes` gate, then the first stderr line containing a (non-blank) `fatalSignatures` substring while not being an exact `informationalLines` entry. `isRunnerSpawnFailure(error, runnerProgram, workdir)` attributes only Node `EACCES`/`ENOENT` whose `syscall` equals `spawn <argv[0]>` (or whose `path` equals `argv[0]` with syscall `spawn`), after independently proving the workdir is an executable directory. Foreground runner failure throws `SandboxUnavailableError` (code `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE`); background stamps `runnerFailed` in `onProcessDone`.
invariants: Runner failure outranks denial because the command did not run. Carry the matched fatal line, not an informational line that preceded it. (packages/shell/bash-sandbox/src/index.ts:108-109)
concurrent path replacement may change attribution but cannot permit an unconfined execution. (packages/shell/bash-sandbox/src/helpers.ts:31-33)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed on runner failure (foreground throws `SandboxUnavailableError`, never silently degrades to an unconfined run); fail-soft on plain denial (reported as `denied: true` fact plus a rendered marker).

constants.meaning: EXECUTABLE_SPAWN_CODES — the only Node codes treated as runner-executable evidence; mirrored at packages/shell/pwsh-sandbox/src/helpers.ts:15
exact syscall string required when the error carries no `path`
accepted syscall values when `path === argv[0]`

mechanisms.name: shell-background-process-handle
mechanisms.what: `startArgv(spec, argv)` spawns through `ctx.subprocess` with the executor's own output cap (not the foreground `stdoutMaxBytes`) and returns a `ShellProcess` object literal with `status`/`exitCode`/`signal`, a `done` promise, `readOutput()` and `kill()`. `readOutput` keeps `stdoutOffset`/`stderrOffset` cursors, labels stderr with a `[stderr]` section, propagates `lossy` and the two spill paths, and drains a one-shot `providerFailureNote`. `done` sets `killed` when the caller signal aborted or the process died from a signal, otherwise `completed`; rejection is caught and converted to a `killed` handle.
invariants: `done` settles at process close and never rejects — provider rejection settles as `killed` with a stage-neutral error on stderr. (packages/shell/shell/src/types.ts:168-171)

A still-running background process is stopped and awaited when its owning composition tears down ... so a background process survives an executor-only reload. (packages/shell/shell/src/index.ts:59-62)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft — a provider rejection is caught, `status` becomes `killed`, and the detail is delivered once through `readOutput` as `subprocess failed before reporting an outcome: <detail>`; `done` still resolves.

constants.meaning: ShellProcessStatus union
provider-failure note text — mirrored at packages/shell/pwsh-local/src/index.ts:323
stderr section separator in a background read delta

mechanisms.name: shell-cause-classification-timeout-vs-abort
mechanisms.what: `runArgv` opens ONE fused deadline with `using d = deadline(spec.signal, spec.timeoutMs, 'BASH_TIMEOUT')` and passes `d.signal` into the spawn. After the handle settles it computes `timedOut = timeoutOf(d.signal, 'BASH_TIMEOUT') !== undefined` and `aborted = d.signal.aborted && !timedOut`, and returns those booleans plus the effective `timeoutMs` on the result. The pwsh executor reuses the SAME code string `'BASH_TIMEOUT'`, so bash and pwsh share one timeout dialect.
invariants: Mutually exclusive with aborted: one fused deadline drives both the timeout and the caller's cancellation, so a timeout and an abort racing before process close report the single first-abort cause, not both. (packages/shell/shell/src/types.ts:119-124)
Only this executor's timeout reason counts as timedOut; outer deadlines count as aborts. (packages/shell/bash-local/src/index.ts:231)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft — a timeout or abort resolves with a `ShellRunResult` carrying `timedOut`/`aborted` instead of rejecting; only infrastructure failures reject.

constants.meaning: capability-owned timeout code stamped onto TimeoutReason; reused verbatim by pwsh at packages/shell/pwsh-local/src/index.ts:264
internal no-timer sentinel in `deadline()` (arms no timer, forwards only the upstream signal)

mechanisms.name: shell-output-collection-and-spill
mechanisms.what: Both executors request collect-mode readers (`stdout: collect(stdoutMaxBytes)`, `stderr: collect(config.maxOutputBytes)`) where `collect(maxBytes) = { maxBytes, spill: { maxBytes: config.maxSpillBytes } }`. A settled collect reader is projected by `finalOutput(reader)` calling `reader.readFrom(0)` and mapping `truncated: read.lossy` plus the optional `spillPath`. The in-memory bytes are capped at `maxOutputBytes` and overflow is spilled to a temp file capped at `maxSpillBytes`; larger streams keep only the in-memory tail.
invariants: `run()` uses it for stdout; background jobs and stderr keep the executor's own output cap. (packages/shell/shell/src/types.ts:91-93)
Per-stream spill-file cap; larger streams retain only their in-memory tail. (packages/shell/bash-local/src/index.ts:50-51)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft — truncation never fails the run; it sets `truncated`/`lossy` and optionally a `spillPath`, which the renderers turn into a notice.

constants.meaning: default per-stream in-memory output cap (stdout foreground default and stderr cap)
default per-stream spill-file cap
truncation notice prefix; '(unavailable)' when no spillPath — mirrored at packages/shell/tool-pwsh/src/render.ts:22

mechanisms.name: shell-exit-marker-contract
mechanisms.what: `renderResult`/`renderPwshResult` append, in order: the sandbox denial marker (plus the escalation hint when the composition advertises targets), `[timed out after <ms>ms]`, then `[killed by signal: X]` or `[exit code: N]`. `parseExitStatus` in the shared shell package is the exact inverse: it strips a trailing `\n[killed by signal: ...]` (yielding `signal`) or `\n[exit code: N]` (yielding `exitCode`), otherwise reports a clean `exitCode: 0`. Both tools use the parse result to build the terminal card's exit pill.
invariants: Keep the exit marker last because parseExitStatus anchors there. (packages/shell/tool-bash/src/render.ts:44)

Requiring a leading newline and the end of the string keeps ordinary output that merely ends with marker-like text from matching unless the final line is indistinguishable from a real marker. (packages/shell/shell/src/render.ts:31-33)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft — text without a marker is treated as a clean exit 0 rather than an error.

constants.meaning: signal-marker regex (anchored at end)
exit-code-marker regex (anchored at end)
timeout marker; emitted even when the command trapped SIGTERM and exited 0

mechanisms.name: bash-tool-registration
mechanisms.what: `apply(ctx, config)` in tool-bash reads `ctx.shell.sandboxMode`; if the mounted executor confines it requires `ctx.get('sandboxPolicy')` and throws at plugin load when missing, and derives `escalationModes = ESCALATION_TARGETS` (else `[]`). It registers a system-prompt section `tool:bash` and one `defineTool({name:'bash', ...})` whose parameters are `command`, `description`, `timeoutMs`, `workdir`, plus `run_in_background` and `sandbox_permissions`/`justification` only when advertised. `execute` validates args, resolves the standing sandbox policy, optionally runs the escalation approval, resolves workdir, collects `ctx.shellEnv.collect(exec)`, then either `ctx.jobs.start(...)` or `ctx.shell.run(ctx.shell.resolve({...request, signal: exec.signal}))`. The pwsh package mirrors this call-for-call with `name: 'pwsh'`.
invariants: the mounted bash executor confines but ctx.sandboxPolicy is missing -> throw at tool-plugin load. (packages/shell/tool-bash/src/index.ts:194-196)
Undeclared keys are allowed, so schema omission also needs enforcement. (packages/shell/tool-bash/src/index.ts:349)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — invalid args throw before any spawn; missing `jobs`/`sandboxPolicy` throws; an aborted `exec.signal` throws a `HarnessError('tool call aborted', TOOL_ABORTED)` renamed `AbortError`.

constants.meaning: `enableRunInBackground` default; `false` disables the parameter AND rejects the call at packages/shell/tool-bash/src/index.ts:350-352
system-prompt section names
registered tool names

mechanisms.name: shell-background-job-registration
mechanisms.what: For `run_in_background: true` the tool requires `ctx.get('jobs')`, checks the caller signal, then calls `jobs.start({ kind: 'bash'|'pwsh', label: args.command, owner: exec.agent, run })`. The `run` thunk starts the process with `ctx.shell.start(ctx.shell.resolve(request))` (NO signal — no timeout applies) and returns `{cancel: () => void proc.kill(), done: proc.done.then(() => processOutcome(proc)), readOutput: () => renderProcessRead(...)}`. The tool returns `{kind:'background', jobId}` immediately. `processOutcome` maps `killed` -> `{status:'killed', detail:'signal: X'|'killed before exit'}` and everything else -> `{status:'completed', detail:'exit code: N'}`.
invariants: The caller owns cancellation until ctx.jobs commits detached ownership. (packages/shell/tool-bash/src/index.ts:357)
real nonzero command exits must remain `completed`. (packages/shell/tool-bash/src/background.ts:22)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — missing service or disabled background throws (fail-closed); a spawn failure aliases a signal-less kill and is therefore reported as `killed`, not `failed` (explicit TODO at packages/shell/tool-bash/src/background.ts:18-22).

constants.meaning: job kind registered with ctx.jobs; pwsh uses 'pwsh' at packages/shell/tool-pwsh/src/index.ts:381
output-schema discriminator const for the background handle

mechanisms.name: sandbox-escalation-approval
mechanisms.what: `validateEscalationArgs(sandbox_permissions, justification)` enforces the pairing/non-emptiness rule during arg validation. `approveBashEscalation`/`approvePwshEscalation` first throw if `escalationModes.length === 0`, then delegate to the shared `approveEscalation({requestedMode, justification, effectiveMode, subject:'command'}, {approver: ctx.get('approval'), agent, callId, toolName, signal})`, passing the standing policy's current `mode` as `effectiveMode`. The resolved `SandboxMode` replaces `policy.mode` for the single call.
invariants: This tool contributes only the composition guard ... and the approval ingredients. The shared policy resolver is required whenever the executor advertises confinement, so a split composition fails at tool-plugin load. (packages/shell/tool-bash/src/index.ts:206-211)
an unadvertised `sandbox_permissions` still reaches execute (packages/shell/tool-bash/src/index.ts:207-209)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — no escalation targets => throw; approval outcome mapping is delegated to `approveEscalation`, which is described as a fail-closed sequence (packages/shell/tool-bash/src/index.ts:203-205).

constants.meaning: approval subject; same literal at packages/shell/tool-pwsh/src/index.ts:231
approval request tool identity

mechanisms.name: shell-tool-workdir-resolution
mechanisms.what: `resolveWorkdir` prefers an explicit model `workdir`, resolving a relative one against the session cwd; otherwise it falls back to the session header cwd. In tool-bash the sandbox policy's `workspaceRoot` (if any) wins over the header cwd and is canonicalized with `canonicalPath`, so that the workdir handed to the executor and the confinement root are the same identity; tool-pwsh omits the policy-root branch and uses `exec.agent?.session.header.cwd` directly.
invariants: A resolved sandbox-policy root wins so workdir and confinement use the exact same per-call identity. (packages/shell/tool-bash/src/index.ts:140-142)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft — returning `undefined` leaves the executor's own `config.cwd ?? process.cwd()` defaulting in charge.

mechanisms.name: shell-tool-call-and-result-presentation
mechanisms.what: `presentBashCall` renders a foreground call as a `terminal` card (title = command, cwd passed through) and a background call as a `generic` execute card whose content is the description. `presentBashResult` returns `undefined` unless the result is exactly one text block, renders background acknowledgements and `isError` results as a fenced `console` generic card, and otherwise splits the exit marker off with `parseExitStatus` so the marker becomes the card's exit pill rather than duplicated body text. tool-pwsh mirrors both with arrow-function variants.
invariants: The exit marker becomes the card's exit pill, so it leaves the output body. (packages/shell/tool-bash/src/index.ts:132)

The consumed marker is removed from `body` because a terminal presentation shows the exit status as its own pill: leaving the marker in the output would render the exit twice. (packages/shell/shell/src/render.ts:24-27)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft — an unexpected content shape yields `undefined` (no view) instead of throwing.

constants.meaning: card kinds per call path
fence used for background/error results

mechanisms.name: shell-env-registry
mechanisms.what: `ShellEnvRegistry` installs the `ctx.shellEnv` service (apply() just constructs it). `register(contributor)` runs inside `ctx.effect(...)`: it rejects an empty contributor name, a duplicate contributor name, any declared key that does not start with `DSH_ENV_PREFIX` or whose suffix fails `/^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$/`, any key in `RESERVED_BASH_ENV_KEYS` (`DSH_HOME`, `DSH_SHELL`, `DSH_SESSION_ID`), an empty description, and any key already owned by another contributor; on success it records the contributor and key owners and yields a disposer. `collect(execution)` always emits `{DSH_HOME: <resolved home>, DSH_SHELL: '1'}` and adds `DSH_SESSION_ID` when the execution has an agent, then folds contributors in `name.localeCompare` order, rejecting undeclared or non-string values, and returns a frozen, key-sorted environment overlay. `list()` enumerates declarations without running resolvers.
invariants: The namespace is rebuilt for every model shell call: ambient `DSH_*` values are discarded by the executor, then the registry's current snapshot is injected. (packages/shell/shell-env/src/index.ts:81-83)

TODO(bash-env-list-builtins): Include registry-owned built-ins before diagnostics, prompt, or UI code treats list() as an exhaustive environment catalog. (packages/shell/shell-env/src/index.ts:176-177)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — every validation failure throws, both at registration time and inside `collect` (undeclared key, non-string value), so a misbehaving contributor fails the shell call rather than injecting a wrong variable.

constants.meaning: BASH_ENV_KEY_SUFFIX — required shape of the key text after the DSH_ prefix
value of the built-in DSH_SHELL marker variable

mechanisms.name: timeout-deadline-library
mechanisms.what: The shared timeout module exports `TimeoutReason` (an Error carrying capability-owned `code` + `timeoutMs`), `MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS`, `clampTimeout`, `deadline`, `idleWatchdog`, and `timeoutOf`. `deadline(upstream, timeoutMs, code)` returns `{signal, [Symbol.dispose]}`: `timeoutMs <= 0` arms no timer and forwards only the upstream signal; otherwise it arms `setTimeout` and fuses with `AbortSignal.any([upstream, timer.signal])` so the first aborter's reason wins. `idleWatchdog` re-arms its timer per outstanding `next()` demand and exposes `pulse()` for transport activity that yields no iterator value. `timeoutOf(x, code)` recovers a `TimeoutReason` only when the code matches.
invariants: The library only notifies through abort signals; each capability still owns the mechanism that stops its work and translates timeout reasons into public outcomes. (packages/util/timeout/src/index.ts:2-4)
The signal only notifies, so callers must stop their own work. (packages/util/timeout/src/index.ts:84)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft — expiry aborts a signal with a `TimeoutReason`; nothing is killed by this module, so a caller that ignores the signal keeps running.

constants.meaning: MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS — largest Node timer delay; also the validation ceiling for every delay
the internal no-timer sentinel used for background work
TimeoutReason message format

mechanisms.name: native-command-execfile-runner
mechanisms.what: `runNativeCommand(command, args, signal)` is the single host-command boundary: it wraps `execFile(command, [...args], { encoding: 'utf8', signal, windowsHide: true })` in a Promise and resolves `{stdout, stderr}` on exit 0. On error it rejects with `Object.assign(new Error(error.message, {cause: error}), {code: error.code, stdout, stderr})`, so callers can inspect the exact Node code. The declared contract is that native implementations never invoke a shell.
invariants: Testable command boundary; native implementations never invoke a shell. (packages/util/native-command/src/runner.ts:8, repeated at packages/util/native-command/src/path-opener.ts:17)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — a non-zero exit (or spawn error) rejects and carries `code`/`stdout`/`stderr`; there is no fallback path.

constants.meaning: fixed execFile options

mechanisms.name: native-path-opener
mechanisms.what: `openNativePath`/`openNativeTextFile` dispatch one shell-free command per intent: for `default` on a non-WSL host whose path extension is in `BROWSER_DOCUMENTS` it first tries the default browser (macOS: parse `defaults read com.apple.LaunchServices/com.apple.launchservices.secure` for the `https` handler, then `open -b <bundle>`; Linux: `$BROWSER`); then darwin -> `open` (`-t` for text-editor), win32 -> `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command Invoke-Item -LiteralPath '<path>'`, linux -> WSL `wslpath -w` translation then the Windows opener, else `xdg-open`; an unknown platform throws. `revealNativePath` uses `open -R`/`explorer.exe /select,<fileURL>`/`xdg-open <dirname>`; `canOpenNativePath` and `nativeFileManager` expose capability facts.
invariants: Native implementations never invoke a shell. (packages/util/native-command/src/path-opener.ts:17)
Explorer can exit 1 after delegating to the existing desktop process. (packages/util/native-command/src/path-opener.ts:253)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — a browser-naming failure returns false and silently falls back to the default application (fail-soft, path-opener.ts:60-67); an unsupported platform throws (fail-closed, :154, :262); `explorer.exe` exit code 1 is swallowed as a delegated handoff (:254).

mechanisms.name: persistent-pty-shell-session
mechanisms.what: `tool-bash-persistent` and its pwsh mirror keep one PTY session per owning agent through a private `persistentShells(ctx, config)` registry: `pending: WeakMap<Agent, Promise<TerminalSessionId>>`, `live: Map<Agent, TerminalSessionId>`, `creating: Set<Promise>`, `ownerCleanupInstalled: WeakSet`, and a `lifecycle` AbortController. `get(owner, signal)` fuses the caller signal with the lifecycle signal, spawns `ctx.terminals.spawn(owner, {type: config.backendType, cwd: owner.session.header.cwd}, combinedSignal)`, runs a one-time initialization send (`stty -echo` for bash, a custom `prompt` function for pwsh), and throws if the shell exited or the init send timed out. Each command is wrapped in nonce markers (`__DSH_PERSISTENT_BASH_START_<uuid>__` ... `__DSH_PERSISTENT_BASH_END_<uuid>:<status>`), sent, then polled until the end marker with digits, a session exit, a wait reason, or the deadline. `ctx.effect` cleanup aborts creation and kills every live session.
invariants: Keep the wrapper on one physical line. An interactive bash prints PS2 for embedded newlines before executing the buffer, which would leak terminal prompts and marker source text into the model-facing result. (packages/shell/tool-bash-persistent/src/index.ts:81-83)

The shell may flip to exited between iterations (a fast `exit` can settle the previous send while its exit event is still in flight); re-observing status before the next send closes that gap. (packages/shell/tool-bash-persistent/src/index.ts:313-316)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — a command timeout or abort resets (kills) the owner's shell and returns partial output plus a reset notice; an init or send failure also resets and then rethrows; disposal aborts the lifecycle signal and awaits all creation before killing live sessions.

default `maxOutputChars` before clipping; identical at packages/shell/tool-pwsh-persistent/src/index.ts:487
SCROLLBACK_PAGE_LINES per terminals.read page
POLL_INTERVAL_MS between completion-marker polls
default `backendType` PTY backend
timeout codes passed to `deadline()`

mechanisms.name: owner-serialized-command-queue
mechanisms.what: Both persistent tools wrap each execution in `serialized(owner, operation)`, a per-agent promise chain held in `queues: WeakMap<Agent, Promise<void>>`. The new run is chained onto the prior tail with `prior.then(operation, operation)` (so a rejected predecessor does not block the next call), a swallowing `tail` is stored, and the map entry is deleted in `finally` only when it is still the current tail. `execute` requires `exec.agent` and calls `exec.signal.throwIfAborted()` before entering the queue.
invariants: `prior.then(operation, operation)` — a rejected predecessor must not block the next command for the same owner. (packages/shell/tool-bash-persistent/src/index.ts:394)
if the map entry is no longer the tail, leave it alone (packages/shell/tool-bash-persistent/src/index.ts:400)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — a call without an owning agent throws (`bash requires an owning agent session`), and an already-aborted signal throws before any terminal write.

mechanisms.name: persistent-shell-scrollback-paging-and-truncation
mechanisms.what: `retainedScrollback` rebuilds the full scrollback by paging `ctx.terminals.read(owner, id, {offset, count: 1000})` from the newest page backwards, `unshift`ing older pages and OR-ing each page's `truncated` flag, stopping when a page yields no forward progress (`nextScrollbackOffset` returns undefined or reaches `totalLines`). `maybeTruncate` clips at `maxOutputChars` and appends `TRUNCATED_MESSAGE`; an incomplete capture additionally prepends `LOST_PREFIX_MESSAGE`. `renderCaptured` appends `[Command finished with exit code N]` (bash) or `[exit code: N]` only when non-zero (pwsh); `renderShellExitStatus` emits `[shell killed by signal: X]` / `[shell exited: code N]` / `[shell exited]`.
invariants: One page is enough to find a just-emitted completion marker; the full scrollback is assembled only when a command settles or needs partial output. (packages/shell/tool-bash-persistent/src/index.ts:22-23)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft — a truncated or incomplete capture is still returned, annotated with the clip notice and the 'earliest retained output' note, never as an error.

constants.value: <response clipped><NOTE>To save on context only part of this file has been shown to you. ...</NOTE>
constants.meaning: TRUNCATED_MESSAGE appended on clip

constants.value: '<response clipped><NOTE>The beginning of this command output was dropped by the terminal scrollback limit. The following text is the earliest retained output.</NOTE>\n'
constants.meaning: LOST_PREFIX_MESSAGE prepended to an incomplete capture
TIMEOUT_STATUS_MARKER status trailer

mechanisms.name: pwsh-prompt-sentinel-and-echo-stripping
mechanisms.what: The pwsh persistent tool installs its own prompt (`function prompt { [Console]::Write([char]27 + ']133;D;' + [int]$LASTEXITCODE + [char]7); '__DSH_PERSISTENT_PWSH_PROMPT__ ' }`) so the shell emits an OSC 133;D sequence plus a stable sentinel. `wrapCommand` escapes the model command with backtick doubling (` ` `, `"`, `$`, CR stripped, LF -> `` `n ``, ESC -> `` `e ``) and wraps it in `try { Invoke-Expression

; $__ok = $? } catch { $__ok = $false }` selecting `$LASTEXITCODE` when non-null else 0/1. `commandOutput` strips the PSReadLine echo of the wrapper, `promptCompleted` treats a viewport ending in the sentinel as command end, and `stripPrompt` removes trailing sentinel copies.
invariants: Keep the wrapper on one physical line: PSReadLine renders the echoed input, and a wrapped line would split the echo the extraction strips. (packages/shell/tool-pwsh-persistent/src/index.ts:92-94)

The echoed END nonce can never fabricate completion because the status regex needs digits immediately after it and the echo continues with quote characters. (packages/shell/tool-pwsh-persistent/src/index.ts:94-96)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft — if the start marker scrolled out, extraction falls back to the echoed/streamed text and marks the capture `incomplete` rather than failing; a prompt-terminated send returns partial output.

constants.meaning: SHELL_PROMPT sentinel text (trailing space significant)
OSC 133;D exit-status sequence written by the prompt function
fallback status when $LASTEXITCODE is null

notes: Group A (all of packages/shell/* except the subprocess/terminal/sandbox providers, plus util/native-command and util/timeout). All 20 .ts files in these packages were read in full. Notable cross-package facts: (1) `DSH_ENV_PREFIX` is re-exported from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess` by packages/shell/shell/src/types.ts:13 and used to build the reserved keys at packages/shell/shell-env/src/index.ts:70-72 — its literal value is defined in the subprocess package, not here. (2) `shell/types.ts` explicitly states the vocabulary is owned by the subprocess seam (packages/shell/shell/src/types.ts:3-6). (3) tool-bash-persistent and tool-pwsh-persistent do NOT use `ctx.shell`; they depend only on `ctx.terminals`, so persistent sessions bypass executor config (timeoutMs/maxOutputBytes/graceMs/sandboxMode) entirely. (4) No production caller of `idleWatchdog` was found inside this group; it is exported from packages/util/timeout/src/index.ts:126 — callers, if any, live outside these packages.
